chunks: Or do they have the Unknown, so they write it down?

key_terms.الْغَيْبُ: The Unseen / Hidden knowledge of God

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it asks 'Or do they have the Unseen?'
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Mursalat, this verse challenges the Quraysh polytheists who claimed their idols or tribal leaders possessed exclusive access to divine secrets (Al-Ghayb) to justify their worship. Shia exegesis highlights this as a refutation of the belief that intermediaries or created beings can record and transmit unseen knowledge, emphasizing that true knowledge of the Unseen belongs solely to Allah. The rhetorical question underscores the absurdity of their claim, as they neither possess nor can record what is truly hidden.
